Before Montu: partner manager

At MYOB I helped accountants who'd run desktop software for decades move to the cloud.

Many of my accounting partners had built their practices on MYOB desktop and saw little reason to change. My job was to show them the return on the move in their own terms: hours back, fewer headaches, and a new service to sell.

The move
  • Desktop to cloud. Moving practices from AccountRight desktop files to AccountRight Live, in the cloud.
  • Online ledgers. Helping practices put their own clients on MYOB's online ledgers.
How I showed the return
  • 1:1 practice visits. Demos on their own work, not a generic script.
  • Webinars and partner events. Training for whole practices at once.
  • Time and cost savings. The hours they'd get back from working in one shared, up-to-date file.
  • A new revenue line. Selling online ledgers to their clients as a service.
The same pressure at Best Practice

At MYOB, compliance started the conversation. Single Touch Payroll turned payroll reporting into an online job every pay run, from July 2018 for employers with 20 or more staff and July 2019 for everyone, while tax and BAS lodgement moved online too. Accountants had to change, so my job was to make the move feel like a gain, not a chore.

Best Practice met the same moment in June 2026. The Oxford build carried the new Medicare Assignment of Benefit rules to about 1,500 clinics. Compliance moves practices; good product makes them glad they moved, and I've helped people through that change before.

Montu·CircuitThe old software

Circuit grew for years without anyone asking the people who live in it.

Circuit was the portal Montu's operations teams lived in all day, for orders, patients, approvals and pharmacies. An external agency built it with little business context, and for years new features were bolted on top of old ones. It worked, but it fought the people using it. After the redesign it became Montu admin.

How it was built

No user-centred design

Design was outsourced, and features were added without checking what people needed.

How it was used

Disjointed workflows

Manual steps, several tabs open, and compliance rules tracked in side spreadsheets.

How it looked

No shared standards

Every new screen drifted further from the last, with around 150 accessibility errors on the core screens.

How I work on a backbone system

Map the ripple before the change

Before touching a screen, I map who sits upstream and downstream: an ecosystem map for who is involved, a service blueprint for how the work moves between them.

Judge the flow, not one team

A faster PTX screen only counts if orders still reach pharmacies on time and finance's invoices still reconcile.

Treat data integrity as the product

Billing, stock and compliance all run on what goes in upstream. A bad entry made once is paid for by every team after it.

The same shape at Best Practice. Bp Premier is the backbone of a practice: reception, clinicians and practice managers inside it; Medicare, My Health Record and the immunisation register outside it; partners through Halo Connect. When the Assignment of Benefit rules changed in June 2026, one rule rippled to about 1,500 clinics already on the new build.

How I found what to fix

I started by sitting with the people who use it every day.

4 PTX, patient experience3 PharmOps, pharmacy operations3 Clinical, registered nurses
Understand the work

Interviews and observation

Semi-structured interviews and contextual inquiry to watch real use, plus a Pre-Post score to set a baseline.

Pull the interface apart

Heuristic and accessibility review

Every core screen scored against usability heuristics and Gestalt principles, audited with WebAIM WAVE, and tagged as improve, rewrite or redesign.

Agree what matters

Synthesis and prioritisation

Thematic analysis, peer reviews and prioritisation workshops with delivery and product against OKRs.

Jobs to be done

I built personas from the jobs each team came to Montu admin to do, then mapped their pain points, needs and the other tools they leaned on. The gaps between the job and the software became the roadmap.

jessyuxSource: Montu admin discovery and usability research, Nov 20248 / 13
From old screens to new capabilities

I rebuilt it around the jobs people came to do, not the screens they had.

The jobFind the right patient or order, fast

What it becameSearch by patient ID and the identifiers people use every day, in tables that lead with what matters.

The jobHandle many orders without a tab for each

What it becameDuplicate, order flagging, a status history and bulk actions.

The jobApprove safely without a side spreadsheet

What it becameAP and SAS approvals inside Montu admin, with the visibility that used to live in spreadsheets.

The jobTrust every screen to work the same way

What it becameOne Montu MUI design system, so new screens stop drifting.

Bringing people across

New software only counts once the people who rely on it move with you.

Before each release

Say what is changing, and why

Release notes and comms told each team what was coming and what problem it solved for them.

On their own tasks

Walk teams through it

I showed PTX, PharmOps and the nurses the new flows using the work they do every day.

A step at a time

Phase the rollout

Releases went out in phases up to v1.2, with feedback between each one, so nobody lost a way of working overnight.

Prove it moved

Test with the same people

I re-ran the satisfaction score with the same teams who set the baseline, so the change was measured, not assumed.

What I learned

People leave old software one job at a time, and only when the new way is clearly better.

01

Start with the job, not the feature list

Montu admin improved because it was rebuilt around what each team came to do.

02

Show the return in their numbers

Accountants moved to the cloud when they saw their own hours and revenue, not our roadmap.

03

Bring people with you

Comms, walkthroughs and phased releases turn a forced change into a chosen one.

04

Measure before and after, with the same people

A baseline from the same teams is what makes the improvement believable.

jessyuxSource: Montu admin redesign; MYOB partner management12 / 13
At Best Practice

At Best Practice, I would start by measuring the current journey.

I'd take a data-led approach to continuous retention: find the frictions, then make the journey as easy and seamless as possible, so Best Practice keeps its practices and wins new ones.

  • Frame the big picture with a Lean Canvas. Use a Lean Canvas upfront to get crystal clear on key business drivers, metrics and customer problems before building.
  • Map the whole lifecycle. Audit the Bp Premier journey at its high-friction points, from server updates and the first cloud module through to licence renewal.
  • Build analytics in early. Include tracking requirements in the initial brief so we can see how people use the product right from launch.
  • Keep the data honest. Tag every metric as measured (real-time data), modelled (behavioural forecasts) or estimated (baseline assumptions).
  • Show misses early. Raise misses and drop-offs openly in early sprint reviews, so we can iterate toward a fix quickly.

I'd like to hear what is slowing practices down on the journey to the cloud, or what problems you need solving.
